thread:
Alice M.: quick follow-up — we just had a model fail the intake compatibility sweep (stage: prebench). error is in the validator: mismatch on kv-cache layout and a perf regression on short-sequence decode. :frowning:
Ben K.: ugh. which checks caught it? smoke or full bench?
Alice M.: smoke first — the lightweight prober flagged ~30% higher latency for 1-8 token traffic. full bench then flagged kv-layout incompat on the runtime adapter.
Carla R.: can you paste the small repro? was it quantization-related?
Alice M.: repro: ```bash
curl -X POST https://intake.redwood/api/v1/admit -d '{"model":"gpt-mini-x","input":"hi","mode":"smoke"}'
```
intake-bot: validator: FAIL - kv_cache_schema_mismatch (expected: header_v2, got: header_v1)
Raj P.: that kv header mismatch sounds like an ABI drift from the converter. Did the conversion pipeline change recently?
Carla R.: we pushed a converter perf patch last week that changed how kv segments are emitted (to reduce memory copies). looks like we forgot to bump the admit contract.
Tanya S.: this highlights the interface boundary problem — validator currently assumes a static kv header version. we need either versioned handshake or a capability flag in the admission metadata.
Ben K.: tradeoffs: add handshake (slow but explicit) vs piggyback capability flags (fast but brittle). I'd prefer a tiny handshake on first warmup request for private/dedicated, opt-in for hosted to save latency.
Alice M.: agreed. Also the smoke vs full bench split caught different issues. Proposal:
- keep the fast smoke (1-8 tokens) in the gateway for quick feedback
- run an async full bench (longer sequences, KV schema checks, quantized decode) in the admit pipeline before marking model "certified"
- add a kv_revision field on model metadata and a short handshake fallback for mismatches

Carla R.: implementation note: kv_revision can be a short UUID; converter emits it into the bundle manifest. validator compares and fails fast. if mismatch, admit returns error code + suggestion to reconvert.
Raj P.: and for rollout: allow a grace window where mismatched models are admitted behind a canary flag for internal teams only (to test perf) — require explicit opt-in.
Tanya S.: long-term: we should refactor validator into two services: fast-safety-gate (in gateway path) and deep-compat (async, richer checks). The deep one can keep heavy benches and golden input traces. This avoids adding latency on hot paths.
Ben K.: +1. also add telemetry that ties failing checks to converter commits so we can track regressions per PR.
Alice M.: follow-ups:
- Carla to add kv_revision to bundle manifest and converter (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Raj to draft canary gating flow and opt-in flag (ETA: Wed)
- Tanya to sketch validator split RFC (will include interface shapes) (ETA: Fri)
- Ben to add a short telemetry spike to map failing validators -> git commits (ETA: Thu)

Carla R.: quick Q: do we want the smoke prober to attempt a tiny schema-compatible fallback (e.g., translate header_v1 -> v2) automatically?
Tanya S.: dangerous. auto-mutation can hide incompat issues. I'd rather return a clear error and offer a converter suggestion. maybe a one-click "autofix and reconvert" in Console but gated.
Raj P.: agree. better UX in Console than silent fixes.
Alice M.: ok locking that down. I'll run a one-off repro and post logs to the intake ticket. :eyes: anyone want to pair on the first iteration of the handshake?
Ben K.: I can pair tomorrow morning for 30m.
Carla R.: I'll be available after lunch.
intake-bot: created ticket #INTAKE-4721 "kv_revision mismatch: gpt-mini-x" assigned to Carla R.
Tanya S.: thanks all. will add RFC stub in #eng-ml-rfcs and link here.
Alice M.: thanks — feels like a good set of incremental changes that avoid a big blocking refactor. :thumbsup:
